metadata.name: kill
metadata.description: Terminate or send signals to processes

installation.note: kill is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: kill sends signals to processes, most commonly used to terminate processes. Despite its name, kill can send various signals (not just termination). The default signal is TERM (15), which requests a process to terminate gracefully. Use killall or pkill to kill processes by name instead of PID.
when_to_use: Stop a specific process by PID

syntax.description: Send signal to process(es) specified by PID(s). Default signal is TERM (15). Multiple PIDs can be specified.

misconceptions.title: kill always kills processes
misconceptions.reality: kill sends signals. The default TERM signal requests graceful shutdown, which processes can ignore or handle. Only KILL (-9) forces immediate termination.
misconceptions.tip: kill (default) = polite request to terminate. kill -9 = force kill (cannot be ignored).

misconceptions.title: kill works on process names
misconceptions.misconception: kill can kill processes by name like kill firefox
misconceptions.reality: kill requires process ID (PID), not name. Use killall firefox or pkill firefox to kill by name, or find PID first with ps aux | grep firefox.
misconceptions.tip: kill needs PID. Use killall or pkill for name-based killing, or ps | grep to find PID first.

common_pitfalls.description: Mistyping PID and killing wrong process
common_pitfalls.solution: Always verify PID with ps first. Use ps aux | grep processname to find correct PID. Double-check before killing.

common_pitfalls.description: Using force kill (-9) before trying normal kill
common_pitfalls.solution: Always try normal kill first (kill PID). Only use kill -9 if normal kill doesn't work. Force kill prevents cleanup and may cause data loss.
Be careful with system PIDs (low numbers). Check what process is before killing. Use killall/pkill with caution.

common_pitfalls.description: Using wrong PID or PID that no longer exists
common_pitfalls.solution: Use ps aux | grep processname to find PID. The PID is in the second column. Verify it's the correct process.

best_practices: Always verify PID with ps before killing: ps aux | grep processname
Try normal kill first (kill PID), only use kill -9 if it doesn't work
Use kill -l to see all available signals
Use killall or pkill for name-based killing instead of finding PID
Only kill your own processes unless you have sudo
Be careful with system processes - verify what you're killing
Use kill -HUP to reload daemon configuration instead of kill/restart
performance_tips: kill is instant - signals are sent immediately
Use killall/pkill for faster name-based process management
Combining with pgrep: kill $(pgrep firefox) to kill by name via PID

additional_notes.signals: kill sends signals, not direct termination. Default TERM (15) requests shutdown, KILL (9) forces it.
additional_notes.pid_requirement: kill requires process ID (PID). Use ps, pgrep, or top to find PIDs, or use killall/pkill for name-based killing.
additional_notes.signal_names: Signals can be specified by number (-9) or name (-KILL). Both are equivalent.
additional_notes.permissions: You can only kill your own processes. Use sudo for system processes or other users' processes.
additional_notes.common_signals: TERM (15) = graceful termination, KILL (9) = force kill, HUP (1) = reload config, INT (2) = interrupt (Ctrl+C)
